newsitem.title: Australia: Cricket-Australia fast bowler Craig McDermott retires.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Australia fast bowler Craig McDermott retires.

text.p: Craig McDermott, Australia's second most successful test bowler, on Thursday announced his retirement from all levels of cricket.
McDermott, 31, told a news conference he no longer had the desire to attempt another comeback due to a chronic knee injury and increased business interests.
"Basically I'm out of comebacks," McDermott told reporters at the Gabba cricket ground.
"I've had four (comebacks) and I've returned from all of them stronger, but this time the desire is not there," he said.

Despite being regarded as a fitness fanatic, injury forced McDermott to return home five times from overseas tours. The latest was last February during the World Cup in India, where he broke down with a torn right calf muscle after bowling three overs in a match against Kenya.
McDermott also suffered an ankle injury while jogging during Australia's tour of West Indies in 1995. Australia went on to capture the Frank Worrell trophy on that tour despite the loss of McDermott.
He also returned home after suffering illness or injury during tours of England, South Africa and New Zealand.
The strapping right-arm fast bowler made his first-class debut in the 1983/84 season and first appeared for Australia at the age of 19 in the 1984 Boxing Day test against West Indies.
His career tally of 291 wickets in 71 tests at an average of 28.63 puts him second only to Dennis Lillee as Australia's most prolific test wicket-taker.
Lillee captured 355 wickets at 23.92 in 70 tests.
McDermott took 677 first-class wickets in 174 appearances at an average of 28.1, including four 10 wicket hauls.
